seo.title: Paradise Valley Agadir | Palm Gorge & Natural Pools | MoroccoTripMap
seo.description: Paradise Valley near Agadir: palm-lined gorge, natural pools and an Anti-Atlas day trip inland from the coast.
seo.keywords: Paradise Valley Agadir, Paradise Valley Morocco, palm gorge, natural pools Agadir

overview.title: Palm gorge beyond the beach
overview.p1: Paradise Valley cuts into the Anti-Atlas foothills northeast of Agadir. Palm trees, rock pools and a riverbed path make it a popular escape from the city heat — especially from spring to autumn.
overview.p2: Most visitors come with a driver or small tour. Wear shoes with grip; the walk to the best pools can involve uneven rocks. Bring water and expect limited facilities.

food.title: Eat on the trip
food.p1: Simple cafés and tagine stops exist near the valley entrance — many day tours include a lunch stop. Carry snacks and water regardless.
food.li1: Basic cafés near the access point.
food.li3: Return to Agadir for a fuller dinner.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Private taxi or organised day trip from Agadir is the usual option. Agree the full price including waiting time.

2.title: Footwear
2.desc: Closed shoes with grip — the pool paths are rocky and can be slippery.

3.title: Heat
3.desc: Start early in summer. Shade is limited outside the palm clusters.

q1.question: How far is Paradise Valley from Agadir?
q1.answer: Roughly 1–1.5 hours by road depending on traffic and the exact drop-off point.

q2.question: Do I need a guide?
q2.answer: Not mandatory, but a local driver who knows the path helps. Walking shoes matter more than a guide for fit visitors.

q3.question: Can you swim?
q3.answer: In the natural pools when water levels allow — never dive, and check depth.

q4.question: Is it suitable for children?
q4.answer: Possible with care on rocky sections; not an easy pushchair site.

q5.question: Best season?
q5.answer: Spring and autumn. Summer is hot; winter pools are cooler and quieter.
